recipes.name: Scan with all templates
recipes.summary: Run the full template set against one target. Thorough, and the usual first pass.
recipes.when: Any target you are allowed to test, when you want everything checked.

recipes.name: Known CVEs only
recipes.summary: Run just the CVE templates, the quickest route to a known-vulnerable version.
recipes.when: You want known vulnerabilities, not misconfigurations and info.

recipes.name: High and critical severity
recipes.summary: Only templates rated high or critical, to cut straight to what matters.
recipes.when: A first triage pass, or a target you can only hit briefly.

recipes.name: Technology detection
recipes.summary: Run the technology-detection templates to fingerprint what the target runs.
recipes.when: Early recon, before deciding which deeper templates to run.

recipes.name: Scan a list of hosts
recipes.summary: Read targets from a file, cap the rate, and run across many hosts.
recipes.when: You have many hosts and want to sweep them politely.
recipes.cost: Scales with the list and the rate limit.

recipes.name: Save JSONL output
recipes.summary: Write findings as JSON lines, the format most downstream tools expect.
recipes.when: You want the output structured for a pipeline or report.
recipes.cost: Same as the scan it runs.

recipes.name: Through a proxy
recipes.summary: Route requests through an intercepting proxy so you can watch and replay them.
recipes.when: You want the traffic in Burp or ZAP.

recipes.name: Rate-limited and quiet
recipes.summary: Cap requests per second and concurrency, for a target with monitoring.
recipes.when: You would rather not trip rate alarms.
